title: Ψιττακὸς καὶ γαλῆ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 355. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ψιττακόν τις ἀγοράσας ἀφῆκεν ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας νέμεσθαι.
sentences.tr: Psittakon tis agorasas aphēken epi tēs oikias nemesthai.
sentences.l: A certain man, having bought a parrot, let it loose to range about the house.
sentences.n: νέμεσθαι is the grazing verb again, used loosely of an animal left to go where it likes indoors. Parrots came to the Greek world from India after Alexander's campaigns and were still an expensive curiosity — which is why the bird has just been bought at market.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ τῇ ἡμερότητι χρησάμενος, ἀναπηδήσας ἐπὶ τὴν ἑστίαν ἐκάθισε, κἀκεῖθεν τερπνὸν ἐκεκράγει.
sentences.tr: Ho de tēi hēmerotēti chrēsamenos, anapēdēsas epi tēn hestian ekathise, kakeithen terpnon ekekragei.
sentences.l: And he, having made use of his tameness, having leapt up onto the hearth, sat down, and from there was crying out delightfully.
sentences.i: The parrot made the most of his tameness, hopped up onto the hearth and settled there, and from there called out prettily.
sentences.n: ἐκεκράγει is the pluperfect of κέκραγα, and κέκραγα is a perfect with present force ('I am in full cry'); its pluperfect therefore carries the force of an imperfect, 'he kept crying out'. χράομαι takes the dative of what one makes use of. κἀκεῖθεν is καὶ ἐκεῖθεν by crasis, and τερπνόν is an adjective doing adverbial duty. The ἑστία is the household hearth, the ritual centre of the house — an impudent place for a new bird to install itself.

sentences.t: Γαλῆ δὲ θεασαμένη ἐπυνθάνετο αὐτοῦ τίς τέ ἐστι καὶ πόθεν ἦλθεν.
sentences.tr: Galē de theasamenē epynthaneto autou tis te esti kai pothen ēlthen.
sentences.l: And a weasel, having caught sight of him, was asking him who he was and whence he had come.
sentences.n: πυνθάνομαι takes the genitive of the person questioned (αὐτοῦ). The indirect questions keep the tense and mood of the words as they would have been spoken — ἐστι and ἦλθεν, not the past tenses English shifts to. Weasels were kept in Greek houses as mousers, in the place a cat would later take.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· « Ὁ δεσπότης με νεωστὶ ἐπρίατο.
sentences.tr: Ho de eipen· « Ho despotēs me neōsti epriato.
sentences.l: And he said: « The master bought me lately.
sentences.n: ἐπριάμην serves as the aorist of ὠνέομαι, 'buy', which has none of its own. The speech opens with « and is never closed here: Chambry marks the change of speaker with the dash that begins the next sentence, and leaves the guillemet hanging. It looks like an error and is not — the same shape occurs across the collection.

sentences.t: — Οὐκοῦν, ἰταμώτατε ζῴων, ἔφη, πρόσφατος ὢν τοιαῦτα βοᾷς, ὅτε ἐμοὶ τῇ οἰκογενεῖ οὐκ ἐπιτρέπουσιν οἱ δεσπόται, ἀλλ’ ἐάν ποτε τοῦτο πράξω, προσαγανακτοῦντες ἀπελαύνουσί με. »
sentences.tr: — Oukoun, itamōtate zōiōn, ephē, prosphatos ōn toiauta boāis, hote emoi tēi oikogenei ouk epitrepousin hoi despotai, all’ ean pote touto praxō, prosaganaktountes apelaunousi me. »
sentences.l: — Then, most impudent of animals, she said, newly come as you are, you cry out such things, when to me, the house-born, the masters do not allow it, but if ever I do this, they take it ill besides and drive me off. »
sentences.i: « So, you most brazen of creatures, » she said, « newly bought as you are, you make that noise — when the masters will not allow it to me, who was born in the house; and if I ever do it they take offence and drive me out. »
sentences.n: The quarrel is a slave household's quarrel over standing. πρόσφατος, 'freshly come, new-arrived', picks up the parrot's own νεωστὶ ἐπρίατο; οἰκογενής, 'born in the house', is said of the slave raised in it, who ranked higher and expected more licence. ἰταμώτατε ζῴων is a superlative in the vocative with a partitive genitive, 'most impudent of animals'. ἐπιτρέπω takes the dative of the person permitted. The dash that opens the sentence is Chambry's mark for the change of speaker; the weasel is talking now.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· « Οἰκοδέσποινα, ἀλλὰ σύ γε βάδιζε μακράν· οὐχ ὁμοίως γὰρ δυσχεραίνουσιν οἱ δεσπόται ἐπὶ τῇ ἐμῇ φωνῇ ὅσον ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ. »
sentences.tr: Ho de apekrinato legōn· « Oikodespoina, alla sy ge badize makran· ouch homoiōs gar dyscherainousin hoi despotai epi tēi emēi phōnēi hoson epi tēi sēi. »
sentences.l: And he answered, saying: « Mistress of the house, but you at any rate, walk far off; for the masters are not vexed at my voice in the same measure as at yours. »
sentences.i: And the parrot answered: « Mistress of the house, take yourself well away; the masters are not put out by my voice as they are by yours. »
sentences.n: Οἰκοδέσποινα, 'lady of the house', is mock deference: the weasel has just claimed the standing of the house-born, and the parrot hands her the title. δυσχεραίνω with ἐπί and the dative is 'to be put out at' a thing. οὐχ ὁμοίως … ὅσον yokes two halves of different comparisons together, 'not equally … as much as' — loose, but perfectly clear.

sentences.t: Πρὸς ἄνδρα πονηροψόγον ἑτέροις ἀεὶ αἰτίας προσάπτειν ἐπιχειροῦντα ὁ λόγος εὔκαιρος.
sentences.tr: Pros andra ponēropsogon heterois aei aitias prosaptein epicheirounta ho logos eukairos.
sentences.l: Against a man given to malicious fault-finding, always attempting to fasten blame on others, the story is well-timed.
sentences.i: The story is well aimed at the man who carps out of malice and is forever trying to fix the blame on somebody else.
sentences.n: The εὔκαιρος formula, naming whom the fable is aimed at rather than stating a rule; πρός with the accusative here is hostile, and no copula is written — ἐστί is left to be understood, as regularly in these morals. πονηρόψογος is a rare compound of πονηρός and ψόγος, 'blame', and means the blamer whose blaming is itself the base thing. προσάπτω takes the dative of the person the charge is fastened to.
